label: D25-pseudonim-audit
decision: How should Anastrophe's append-only, per-site hash-chained audit log (ADR-0024) satisfy the SDD rules that audit rows are pseudonymized on account deletion (HMAC user id, NFR-PR03) and retained 1 year (≤ 5 years), given that rows cannot be updated and verification currently starts at seq 1?

candidates.description: Write only pseudonymous actor/subject ids from the start: device/credential UUIDs today, and for future user/admin identities a per-site HMAC pseudonym computed at write time with a key held outside the audit table. Account deletion destroys the user-to-pseudonym mapping instead of rewriting rows, so rows stay immutable and hashes stay valid. Retention purges whole leading segments and verification resumes from a stored checkpoint (seq, hash) recorded before the purge.

Change the hash input to cover a digest of each identity field instead of the field itself, so a privileged job can later replace the identity value with a pseudonym (with the trigger temporarily disabled) without breaking verification. Requires a controlled UPDATE path on an otherwise append-only table.
Encrypt identity fields per user with a per-user key stored elsewhere; account deletion destroys the key (crypto-shredding). Rows and hashes stay unchanged because the ciphertext is hashed.

priorities: 1) Satisfy the SDD/NFR-PR03 privacy rules (pseudonymization on deletion, bounded retention). 2) Keep audit rows immutable and tamper-evident (FR-54, ADR-0024). 3) Keep the design simple and consistent with the existing per-site HMAC practice (CLAUDE.md rule 6). 4) Decide before any production row exists. The user approved autonomous iteration; decisions under 0.60 go back to the user.
requirements: Account deletion leaves no directly identifying user value in any audit row, without updating or deleting audit rows.
Every remaining audit row stays verifiable after account deletion and after retention purges.
No UPDATE path on audit_events is needed in normal operation.
